data_and_models: No training of their own: on-device Whisper (ASR) and Vall-E-X (TTS + cloning), quantised/pruned via Qualcomm AI Hub to reach DSP and GPU paths. Nothing in the capture says how voice-clone consent or audio retention is handled.

same comparison; measurement method not stated

one_line: Local A.I voice generation and transformation, powered by Qualcomm.

sections.accomplishments: Reported up to 2x faster transcription and ~35% lower power draw on Snapdragon X versus the unoptimised path; modular design so new voices, languages and audio effects can be added without a rewrite.
sections.challenges: Getting Whisper onto Snapdragon X's DSP and GPU required the AI Hub optimisation pipeline; quantisation and pruning had to be balanced against transcription accuracy; the UI had to stay usable while exposing voice cloning.
sections.how_we_built_it: FastAPI pipeline around Qualcomm Whisper for ASR and Vall-E-X for TTS/voice cloning; Whisper weights optimised and quantised through Qualcomm AI Hub so the DSP/GPU paths are used; React frontend for Windows.
sections.inspiration: Cloud TTS forces a trade between privacy, latency and cost, and nobody teaches the on-device path. They targeted people who already have finished material and no interest in learning prompt tooling.
sections.learned: Quantisation plus hardware-specific kernels move on-device performance more than model choice does; local-first wins on latency, privacy and cost simultaneously.
sections.what_it_does: Windows app with two modes: generate speech from text using one of five built-in voices or a cloned voice, or re-voice any uploaded or recorded clip. Transcription and synthesis both run on the Snapdragon X device.
sections.what_next: Emotional intonation and prosody controls, ports to other Snapdragon devices, partnerships with assistive-technology and healthcare users.

testing: No test suite or eval harness is described; the numbers above are self-reported without a stated benchmark.
